features.name: Custom Agents
features.slogan: Teach it your way. Put it to work.
features.role: Operators and teams with repeatable tasks
features.problem: Useful work gets described from scratch, and each result needs the same corrections.
features.intro: Start with a ready-to-use agent or describe a new one. Refine its instructions, tools, and output through conversation, then save the approach that meets your needs. Agents can serve general tasks as well as NIMBL workflows.
features.request: Create a daily syslog agent. Group repeated events and keep the source records.
features.story: A network operator starts with the included Daily Syslog Summary Agent, asks for a shorter priority summary, checks the revised report, and saves those instructions for tomorrow.
features.outcome: A reusable agent with a defined task and inspectable output.
features.prereq: A working model and the tools/data required by the task. NIMBL is needed only for NIMBL tasks.
features.boundary: Changing instructions is not model training or proof of better accuracy. The first Milestone validates the syslog workflow; other tasks require their own validation.

features.name: Site History & Knowledge
features.problem: Important observations and previous resolutions are scattered across logs, reports, and people.
features.intro: Retain important observations, syslogs, changes, and investigation findings under defined retention rules. Retrieve the evidence when a new issue appears, with its source and time context.
features.request: Has this issue happened before? What changed before it started, and what helped last time?
features.story: Daily syslog-reviewer and device-snapshot retain evidence; incident-investigator combines the records for a recurring-link investigation initiated through Ask nimbls.
features.outcome: An incident timeline and a comparison with previous cases, including source references and unresolved questions.
features.prereq: Accessible historical records, retention rules, identity/time consistency, and supported retrieval operations.
features.boundary: Saving reports alone is not historical understanding. A similar event or correlated change does not establish root cause.

features.name: Local AI
features.slogan: Everyday work. Close to your data.
features.problem: Routine analysis may depend on external inference even when data and compute can stay on site.
features.intro: Run supported models on your computer or an approved site server. Validate useful network and general-purpose workflows locally, with explicit model and hardware requirements.
features.request: Use our local model to compare these documents and highlight the differences.
features.story: An operations team needs to summarize internal network events and compare confidential maintenance documents. It selects an approved on-site model, runs both tasks locally, and reviews the reports alongside evidence that no external inference request was made. If the model cannot finish a task, the intended local-only behavior is to report the limitation instead of silently sending the data to a cloud model.
features.outcome: A locally generated network report and a document comparison with references to the supplied files.
features.prereq: Provisioned local model, sufficient hardware, and compatible tool capabilities. Offline tasks need their dependencies available locally.
features.boundary: Local deployment does not automatically mean local inference. Hardware and operation have costs; do not promise zero cost or universal model quality.

securityAdvantages.title: Keep sensitive inputs on site
securityAdvantages.description: For validated local-only workflows, prompts, supplied documents and network evidence are processed by a model on your computer or an approved site server, without sending them to an external inference provider.

securityAdvantages.title: Reduce external data exposure
securityAdvantages.description: Keeping routine inference local reduces the number of external services that receive task content and the provider data-handling arrangements your team must assess for that workflow.

securityAdvantages.title: Use infrastructure your team controls
securityAdvantages.description: Run inference within your approved environment, where your IT team can apply its own network access, identity, storage and retention controls. These protections depend on how the environment is configured.

securityAdvantages.title: Keep external assistance a deliberate choice
securityAdvantages.description: Local-only work must not silently fall back to a cloud model. Controlled external assistance is planned separately for Milestone 6, with data-type review, permitted destinations and disclosure checks before enablement.

features.securityLimits: Local inference is one part of data protection. Agent tools, telemetry, updates and other integrations require separate network review. Local files and reports still need appropriate access controls, retention and backups. A local interface alone does not prove local processing or an air-gapped deployment.
features.salesExplanation: Put AI to work where your sensitive data already lives. Local AI is designed to analyze internal network evidence and documents using an approved on-site model, reducing exposure to external inference providers. Your team controls the surrounding infrastructure. We demonstrate the benefit by completing representative tasks and checking that no external inference requests occur; controlled external assistance is a separate future capability.

features.name: Scheduling & Automation
features.slogan: Set the task. Keep it working.
features.role: People repeating the same checks and reports
features.problem: A useful reporting workflow still depends on someone remembering to start it every day.
features.intro: Schedule a tested agent and inspect each outcome. Adjust, pause, resume, or cancel its schedule without confusing the schedule with an active execution.
features.request: Run this report every morning at 8 a.m. in our saved timezone.
features.story: After refining the daily report, an operator saves a schedule, checks the next due time, and inspects the following execution. A failed run remains visible even when an older report is available.
features.outcome: A saved daily schedule with next due time and visible execution outcomes.
features.prereq: Saved agent and working dependencies; application running and computer awake when due.
features.boundary: Missed occurrences are not caught up. Pausing or cancelling a schedule does not stop an already running task.
benefits: See failures and skipped work clearly

features.name: Results Center
features.slogan: Work becomes something you can use.
features.role: People who review, share, and reuse agent deliverables
features.problem: Useful results are hard to find again or are trapped in a conversation.
features.intro: Browse and pin reports, request revisions, and preserve useful deliverables. Later add interactive HTML, report search, organization, and archiving with explicit retention behavior.
features.request: Find last month’s incident reports and archive older reports while keeping important cases searchable.
features.story: A service lead finds a set of incident reports, inspects an interactive summary, and asks to archive older material. The team can still retrieve the retained important cases.
features.outcome: A usable report collection with an interactive view and retrievable archived material.
features.prereq: Output operations and metadata. Advanced search, preview isolation, and retention semantics must be implemented.
features.boundary: Markdown browsing/pinning and prior-file archiving remain in Milestone 1. Full version-diff/restore UI is not promised. Report content and execution status remain distinct.

features.name: Agent Improvement Review
features.slogan: Learn from the work. Improve the next run.
features.role: Agent owners reviewing quality and consistency
features.problem: Repeated errors are hard to fix without knowing which inputs, instructions, and results produced them.
features.intro: Ask nimbls to inspect an agent’s retained execution evidence and propose a targeted change. Compare results before adopting the revised approach.
features.request: This agent missed an important event. Review its work and help me improve it.
features.story: An operator supplies a known missed event. Ask nimbls examines the relevant work, suggests a change to the reporting instructions, and compares the revised behavior on the missed case and previously successful cases.
features.outcome: A review explaining the proposed change, before/after results, and remaining limitations.
features.prereq: Queryable work history, retained evidence, editable agent settings, and representative evaluation cases.
features.boundary: This is evidence-based refinement, not automatic self-improvement or model training. Missing history may prevent a reliable conclusion.

features.name: Controlled External Assistance
features.role: Teams needing advanced analysis with controlled disclosure
features.problem: Complex questions may benefit from stronger models, but the complete site history or raw data cannot simply be sent away.
features.intro: Let the local agent request bounded assistance from an approved external model. The proposed nimbls Relay supports controlled routing; enforce disclosure policy before data leaves the site and validate advice locally.
features.request: Ask for a second opinion using only the evidence our policy allows.
features.story: A local investigation remains inconclusive. The agent prepares minimal evidence, applies the configured rules and required approval, then requests external analysis. Any request for more data passes through the same local checks.
features.outcome: An external contribution with provenance, policy outcome, and a locally qualified analysis.
features.prereq: Local workflow, reviewed/tested policies for each enabled data type, approved provider/route, and verified recipient handling.
features.boundary: Relay architecture remains a proposal. Unknown data types are blocked. External advice grants no device permissions. Do not promise zero leakage, zero retention, or free frontier-model use.
benefits: Keep site authority with the local agent

features.name: Execution Management
features.slogan: See the work. Stay in control.
features.role: People supervising agent work and device operations
features.problem: A finished conversation does not prove that the task succeeded or a device reached the intended state.
features.intro: Inspect progress, stop or rerun work, and distinguish successful results from incomplete attempts. Extend this foundation to authorized device changes with before/after verification.
features.request: Apply this supported change to these devices, then verify what actually changed.
features.story: An operator defines a supported change and device scope. The Device Change Agent explains the intended action, uses authorized operations, and checks actual state. Partial failures are reported separately with the required next steps.
features.outcome: A change record with authorized scope, before/after observations, per-device outcomes, and recovery needs.
features.prereq: Supported NIMBL/bbcli operation, enforceable authorization, observable device state, and an operation-specific recovery plan.
features.boundary: Progress, Stop, rerun, and truthful failures start in Milestone 1. Milestone 7 does not promise universal autonomous repair or rollback support for every device operation.
benefits: Verify results beyond a success message

agentFeatures.title: Daily syslog review
agentFeatures.scope: Run scripts first to classify known patterns, deduplicate events and count changes by device and time. The agent reviews unmatched logs and unusual changes in known patterns, then retains useful, critical and anomalous findings.
agentFeatures.marketingTitle: Know what matters in your network.
agentFeatures.marketingDescription: Reviews your network’s syslogs every day and highlights important events, unusual activity, and recurring issues.

agentFeatures.title: Daily device snapshots
agentFeatures.scope: Use a script to capture a defined snapshot of every in-scope device and store it through a shared database interface. Compare snapshots; let the agent explain meaningful differences and recommend retention changes.
agentFeatures.marketingDescription: Keeps a daily record of your devices and highlights changes worth your attention.

agentFeatures.title: Evidence-backed incident investigation
agentFeatures.scope: On request, combine retained syslog findings, device snapshots and previous cases into an incident timeline. Cite evidence, explain possible causes and identify missing information.
agentFeatures.marketingTitle: Find answers in your site’s history.
agentFeatures.marketingDescription: Connects current issues with past events and device changes to help explain what happened and what to check next.

agentFeatures.title: Site operations entry point
agentFeatures.scope: Extend the existing Milestone 1 agent to answer site-history questions, inspect daily-agent outcomes, initiate a scoped investigation and help refine schedules or review candidate patterns. Daily jobs continue independently on their schedules.
agentFeatures.marketingTitle: Your site knowledge. One place to ask.
agentFeatures.marketingDescription: Answers questions about your network, checks your agents’ work, and helps you take the next step.

items.title: Google Workspace
items.promise: Bring your email, calendar, and files into one useful briefing.
items.potentialScope: Gmail, Google Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Slides.
items.exampleRequest: Summarize customer emails, check tomorrow’s meetings, and find the documents I need.
items.outcomes: Email summaries, draft replies, meeting preparation, and document lookup.
items.readiness: Existing Pi integrations identified; nimbls compatibility remains untested.

items.title: Microsoft 365
items.promise: Turn everyday office information into a clear next step.
items.potentialScope: Outlook mail and calendar, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams, and Excel.
items.exampleRequest: Prepare me for tomorrow’s customer meeting using relevant emails, files, and team updates.
items.outcomes: Meeting briefs, email drafts, shared-file search, and spreadsheet summaries.
items.readiness: Microsoft Graph is a candidate integration route; connector selection and nimbls validation are pending.

items.title: Web research
items.promise: Get a sourced answer without opening dozens of tabs.
items.potentialScope: Public websites, product documentation, and news sources.
items.exampleRequest: Compare these three products and give me a short brief with source links and dates.
items.outcomes: Research briefs, product comparisons, and summaries of changes on selected pages.
items.readiness: Suggested for evaluation; source access, freshness, and citation quality need validation.

items.title: Documents & spreadsheets
items.promise: Turn scattered files into something you can use.
items.potentialScope: User-selected PDFs, text documents, spreadsheets, and CSV files.
items.exampleRequest: Compare these proposals and turn the prices, differences, and open questions into a table.
items.outcomes: Document comparison, data cleanup, summaries, and reusable reports.
items.readiness: Suggested for evaluation; builds on the planned document-comparison direction. Format support and output quality need validation.

items.title: Team chat & task tracking
items.promise: Turn conversations into follow-ups people can act on.
items.potentialScope: Potential services include Slack, Teams, Jira, Asana, and Trello; the final service list is undecided.
items.exampleRequest: Summarize this project discussion and draft follow-up tasks with owners and due dates.
items.outcomes: Discussion summaries, task drafts, and project status updates.
items.readiness: Suggested for evaluation; start with one chat service and one task service. Teams overlaps with Microsoft 365.

items.title: Customer & CRM follow-ups
items.promise: Prepare the next customer conversation with the right context.
items.potentialScope: Potential services include HubSpot or Salesforce, alongside a connected email account.
items.exampleRequest: Review this customer’s recent activity and draft a follow-up with the next steps.
items.outcomes: Customer briefs, follow-up drafts, and proposed CRM updates.
items.readiness: Exploratory candidate; choose a service and validate account access and supported actions first.
